description: Labelled columns for B2 (GUARDRAILS.md Tier B, issue #50). Each table is one ClassificationRequest; each column carries the labels a correct classifier must produce. Hard negatives are the point: a fixture of obvious positives measures nothing a regex could not do.

columns.name: email
columns.why: a direct contact identifier; name, format and semantic type all agree

columns.name: email_domain
columns.why: HARD NEGATIVE. The name contains 'email' and the values look like domains, but 9 distinct values over 48k rows cannot re-identify anyone. Low cardinality is the evidence; a classifier keying on the name alone labels this pii.

columns.name: ssn_hash
columns.why: HARD NEGATIVE. 'ssn' in the name, but a 64-character opaque digest at full cardinality is a hash, not a national identifier. Decided from name, length and shape together — the semantic type deliberately says only 'text' and gives nothing away.

columns.name: full_name
columns.why: a person's name; no semantic type identifies it, so it must be read from the name and the masked shape

columns.name: signup_source
columns.why: a low-cardinality enum; nothing about a person

columns.name: card_number
columns.why: MULTI-LABEL. A payment instrument and, tied to a cardholder, re-identifying. A classifier forced to pick one label loses information the schema allows it to keep.

columns.name: amount_cents
columns.why: a transaction amount tied to a party

columns.name: currency_code
columns.why: HARD NEGATIVE. Sits in a financial table beside financial columns, but a currency code is not itself financial data about anyone. Guilt by association is the error this catches.

columns.name: test_card_number
columns.why: HARD NEGATIVE. Synthetic data: the semantic type says credit_card and the shape matches, but 5 distinct values across 121k rows in a column named 'test_' is a fixture, not a customer's card. The strongest signal (semantic_type) points the wrong way on purpose.

columns.name: settled_at
columns.why: a timestamp; not sensitive on its own

columns.name: patient_mrn
columns.why: MULTI-LABEL. A medical record number identifies a patient in a clinical context: a provider identifier and a person identifier at once.

columns.name: diagnosis_code
columns.why: a diagnosis about an identifiable person; phi without being pii on its own

columns.name: department_code
columns.why: HARD NEGATIVE. A clinical table's low-cardinality organisational code. Sits beside phi and is not phi.

columns.name: notes_length
columns.why: HARD NEGATIVE with SPARSE EVIDENCE. Derived from clinical notes and named suggestively, but a character count carries no health information. 15% null and nothing but an integer to go on.
